hard: Farid and Nadia went to Green Valley Wildlife Centre on Friday.
Their class arrived at 11 am in a white coach.
There were 12 children in the group.
Nadia wore a red coat and Farid wore a blue cap.
A keeper called Miss Lily met them at the gate.
She led the group past a pond and a small barn.
The first stop was a low wooden pen.
A brown hedgehog lay inside on a bed of straw.
Miss Lily called her Pip.
Pip curled into a tight ball and hid her face.
A hedgehog has about 5000 spines on its back.
The spines help a hedgehog survive danger.
Pip did not bite, and she did not run away.
Next the children walked to a sunny garden.
A large tortoise sat on the warm grass.
Miss Lily called him Gus.
Gus ate a green lettuce leaf very slowly.
A giant tortoise lives for more than 100 years.
Gus did not hide in his shell, and he walked up to the children.
Inside the small barn, a glass box stood on a table.
A grey mouse sat in the box with white seeds.
The mouse chewed a seed and washed its face.
The front teeth of a mouse grow all through its life.
Chewing keeps the teeth short.
The next room was dark and cool.
Miss Lily turned on a purple lamp.
A scorpion glowed under the lamp.
A scorpion uses the sting in its tail to kill insects.
Farid stepped back, but Nadia stayed close to the glass.
Nadia took a photo, but the scorpion did not move.
The last show was outside on the big lawn.
It lasted 40 minutes.
A golden eagle flew over the lawn and landed on a tall pole.
An eagle can see a small animal from far away.
Farid clapped and Nadia cheered.
Later the class waved goodbye to Miss Lily.
Nadia bought a card of Pip and Farid bought a card of Gus.
They sat on the coach and talked about the animals.
It was an exciting day at the centre.
